_notes: Generated against the REAL pipeline (tree-sitter + semgrep + dependency scanner + the real normalizer), not hand-guessed — see ecdat-backend/tests/test_scanner.py which regenerates and checks this empirically every run.

expected_assets are algorithms that MUST be detected (recall). negative_cases are constructs that MUST NOT produce any asset (precision / false-positive resistance) — see python/mixed.py's docstring, string-literal algorithm name, and commented-out RSA import+call.

known_gaps documents real, current scanner limitations discovered while building this fixture set, intentionally not asserted as findings so the test suite doesn't lie about what ECDAT can actually see today.

negative_cases.description: docstring prose mentioning 'RSA-like key rotation' and 'legacy MD5 checksums'
string literal DEPRECATED_ALGO_NAME = "MD5" (a value, not a call)

known_gaps: go/certificates.go's tls.Config{CipherSuites: [...]} block is not detected — CRYPTO_PATTERNS has no crypto/tls entry. Only the ECDSA P-256 cert key generation in the same file is found.
python/safe.py's ML-KEM mention in IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md's original fixture spec is omitted — no PQC library has an entry in CRYPTO_PATTERNS, so nothing would be detected either way.

AES key size is only extracted when the call literally states a bit-length (JS: {length: 256}); Go/Python constructing AES from a byte-array (make([]byte, 32), b'0'*32) produce a bare 'AES' asset with no key_size, since that requires evaluating the buffer length, not just reading a literal number out of the call text.
